Header.CaseTitle: Metropolitan Property Holdings Ltd v Artisan Coffee Co Ltd

Counsel.Lead: William Hughes KC; Victoria Wilson (instructed by Slaughter and May)

SummaryOfPosition.Summary: The Appellant landlord seeks possession of commercial premises and arrears of rent, contending that the Respondent tenant has forfeited the lease by reason of persistent breach of covenants including non-payment of rent and unauthorized alterations.

FactsReliedOn.item: The Respondent holds a 15-year lease of retail premises at 45 High Street, Richmond, granted in 2015.
The Respondent has accumulated rent arrears of £87,500 over the period March 2022 to December 2023.
The Respondent carried out structural alterations without the Appellant's consent contrary to clause 4.12 of the lease.
The Appellant served a section 146 notice on 15 January 2024.
The Respondent has persistently paid rent late over the term of the lease.

Contentions.item: The Respondent has committed multiple breaches of covenant entitling the Appellant to forfeit.
The breaches are irremediable given the persistent pattern of non-payment.
Any waiver was limited to the specific rent demands accepted and did not extend to the forfeiture right.
Relief from forfeiture should be refused given the history of breaches.

LegalBasis.item: Landlord and Tenant Act 1954, Part II
